"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

No one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services exists anywhere in the cited text, so the walk-away scenario does not apply; Section 15 also carves Section 13 breaches out of the liability cap and consequential-damages exclusion, which is more favourable than the fallback's 3x super-cap.

Per the playbook's classification semantics, a clause meeting the fallback is compliant and is not redlined; the rationale correctly records the shortfalls versus the preferred position (no express 'defend'/control-of-defence mechanic, no refund remedy, no breach-of-law/data-breach/gross-negligence limbs, affiliates unnamed, tight ten-day notice) as sub-elements rather than fallback failures.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact: the indemnity is triggered by breach of the ownership/no-encumbrance warranty and the same paragraph expressly addresses the consequences where the Work 'is held to constitute an infringement of another Person's rights', so an IP indemnity is in substance present.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is proposed; the finding is properly retained as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

input.rationale: Section 13 contains an express Garman non-infringement warranty backed by an indemnity in our favour covering Losses (including settlement amounts and legal fees) and the usual remedy ladder of procuring rights, substituting an equivalent element, or replacing/modifying the Work (p0090–p0093). There is no reverse indemnity from Sparkling anywhere in the agreement, so the walk-away scenario does not arise, and Section 15 expressly carves breaches of Section 13 out of the liability cap and consequential-damages exclusion, which is better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. This therefore sits at (and in the cap respect above) the fallback position and is not redlined. Noted for information only, short of the preferred position: there is no express "defend"/control-of-defence mechanic, no refund remedy if none of (a)-(c) is achievable, the indemnity is limited to IP/title matters (no breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs), affiliates are not named, and the ten-calendar-day notice requirement is tight — we would take these in negotiation but they are sub-elements rather than fallback failures.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline.**

Section 13, read together with the continuation at p0090–p0093, does contain a genuine vendor-side IP indemnity, despite the heading paragraph (p0087) itself only reciting Garman's ownership:

- **Vendor indemnity present:** Garman warrants it owns/controls all necessary rights with no encumbrances, and agrees to indemnify and hold Sparkling harmless for all Losses (court costs, settlement amounts, reasonable legal fees, investigation costs) from breach of that warranty.
- **Standard remedy ladder:** procure the right, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify so the Work is non-infringing without material loss of functionality.
- **No reverse indemnity:** nothing in the document imposes a Sparkling indemnity for Garman's software or services, so the walk-away case is absent.
- **Better than fallback on cap:** Section 15 states the limitation of liability "shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14" — so the IP indemnity is uncapped and outside the consequential-damages exclusion, exceeding the fallback's 3× super-cap.

Sub-elements short of preferred, noted rather than flagged: no express "defend"/control-of-defence mechanic, no refund fallback remedy, indemnity limited to IP/title (no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross-negligence limbs), affiliates unnamed, and a tight ten-calendar-day notice obligation. These are worth raising in negotiation but do not fail the fallback.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

input.rationale: There is no automatic renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement. Maintenance runs for "a renewable one-year term" (p0065), i.e. a 12-month term that can only be extended by the parties' affirmative agreement, and the licence itself is perpetual so long as fees are paid (p0117). Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling (customer) an unconditional right to terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit cost — 90 days' notice sits at the top of the playbook fallback range (60–90 days) and the absence of any termination fee is better than the fallback cap of three months' fees. Garman has no termination-for-convenience right anywhere in the Agreement: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling on notice under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency/uncured material default under 17(c), and Section 10 maintenance is a renewable one-year term without any Garman right to walk away or suspend at will. Section 17(a) also keeps the licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year lock-in. Noted but not flagged as a deviation: 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund in 17(c)/p0128 applies only on Garman default), which is a sub-element short of the preferred position rather than a failure of the fallback, and fee exposure is limited given the annual maintenance term.

input.quote: The parties agree that the limitation of liability in this paragraph reflects the allocation of risk between the parties and the price of the licenced Software. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only liability provision in the Agreement (no "aggregate liability" language appears anywhere else). It contains a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and carve-outs for Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but no monetary cap of any kind, so each party's — including Sparkling's — exposure for direct damages is unlimited. That fails both the preferred position (mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000) and the fallback (mutual cap of 12 months' fees) on a material term. The redline inserts the mutual cap into the existing sentence, keeps the existing Section 13/14 carve-outs and adds indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement as uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirms our fee payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes. Note that Section 13, despite its caption, contains no actual indemnity; that gap belongs to the indemnity rule rather than this one.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
There is no automatic renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement. Maintenance runs for "a renewable one-year term" (p0065), i.e. a 12-month term that can only be extended by the parties' affirmative agreement, and the licence itself is perpetual so long as fees are paid (p0117). Sparkling may in any event terminate at will on 90 days' notice (p0118), so there is no non-renewal notice window to compute and no risk of lock-in or multi-year auto-renewal. This meets the preferred position (renewal by mutual agreement, 12-month term, easy exit). Two sub-elements fall short of the ideal drafting but are not material deviations: there is no express cap on renewal-period maintenance fee uplift (fees are simply "in accordance with the Fee Schedule"), and no vendor reminder mechanic — we would raise the CPI/3% uplift cap in the Fee Schedule negotiation rather than by redline here.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

The redline inserts the mutual cap into the existing sentence, keeps the existing Section 13/14 carve-outs and adds indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement as uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirms our fee payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes. Note that Section 13, despite its caption, contains no actual indemnity; that gap belongs to the indemnity rule rather than this one.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

input.rationale: There is no automatic renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement. Maintenance runs for "a renewable one-year term" (p0065), i.e. a 12-month term that can only be extended by the parties' affirmative agreement, and the licence itself is perpetual so long as fees are paid (p0117). Sparkling may in any event terminate at will on 90 days' notice (p0118), so there is no non-renewal notice window to compute and no risk of lock-in or multi-year auto-renewal. This meets the preferred position (renewal by mutual agreement, 12-month term, easy exit). Two sub-elements fall short of the ideal drafting but are not material deviations: there is no express cap on renewal-period maintenance fee uplift (fees are simply "in accordance with the Fee Schedule"), and no vendor reminder mechanic — we would raise the CPI/3% uplift cap in the Fee Schedule negotiation rather than by redline here.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Agreement contains no auto-renewal trap for us:

- **§10 (p0065)** — maintenance is provided "For a renewable one-year term," i.e. a 12-month term extendable only by the parties' affirmative agreement. No "automatically renew" language exists anywhere in the document (searches for "renew", "automatically renew" and "increase" returned nothing else).
- **§17(a) (p0117)** — the licence is perpetual so long as fees are paid, so there is no rolling term to escape.
- **§17(b) (p0118)** — Sparkling may terminate at any time on 90 days' written notice, an unconditional customer exit right.

With no automatic renewal there is no non-renewal notice window to compute and no multi-year renewal risk, so this sits at the **preferred** position rather than the fallback.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged (minor sub-elements per the classification rules): there is no express cap on maintenance fee uplift for renewal terms (fees are simply "in accordance with the Fee Schedule"), and no vendor renewal reminder. The CPI/3% uplift cap is better pursued in the Fee Schedule negotiation than by redlining §10.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling (customer) an unconditional right to terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit cost — 90 days' notice sits at the top of the playbook fallback range (60–90 days) and the absence of any termination fee is better than the fallback cap of three months' fees. Garman has no termination-for-convenience right anywhere in the Agreement: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling on notice under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency/uncured material default under 17(c), and Section 10 maintenance is a renewable one-year term without any Garman right to walk away or suspend at will. Section 17(a) also keeps the licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year lock-in. Noted but not flagged as a deviation: 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund in 17(c)/p0128 applies only on Garman default), which is a sub-element short of the preferred position rather than a failure of the fallback, and fee exposure is limited given the annual maintenance term.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant (at fallback).**

Section 17(b) already gives Sparkling a clean convenience exit — termination "at any time" on 90 days' written notice, with no early-termination fee or penalty. That sits at the top of our fallback notice range (60–90 days) and beats the fallback's tolerance for a fee of up to three months' fees.

On the vendor side, Garman has no convenience right at all: Section 17 allows Garman to terminate only for insolvency events or an uncured material default (17(c)), and the Section 10 maintenance term contains no at-will suspension or walk-away right. Section 17(a) keeps the licence perpetual while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year lock-in to escape.

Noted in the rationale but not redlined: 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund at p0128 is limited to termination for Garman's default). That is a sub-element short of our preferred position, not a fallback failure, and exposure is limited by the annual maintenance term — so no redline was proposed.

input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The only governing-law/venue provision (§ 20(h)) selects the laws of Nova Scotia (and Canadian law applicable there) with the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts. Nova Scotia is not among the accepted laws (New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales), so the clause fails the fallback on both material terms (governing law and forum). It is not walk-away territory: the forum is our own home province (Sparkling is in Dartmouth, NS, while Garman is in Saskatoon, SK), the jurisdiction grant is non-exclusive, and there is no arbitration provision anywhere in the agreement. Redline moves the clause to the preferred position (New York law, exclusive New York County courts) while leaving the rest of the sentence structure intact; Delaware, California, or England and Wales/London remains available as a fallback if Garman pushes back.

input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The only governing-law/venue provision (§ 20(h)) selects the laws of Nova Scotia (and Canadian law applicable there) with the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts. Nova Scotia is not among the accepted laws (New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales), so the clause fails the fallback on both material terms (governing law and forum). It is not walk-away territory: the forum is our own home province (Sparkling is in Dartmouth, NS, while Garman is in Saskatoon, SK), the jurisdiction grant is non-exclusive, and there is no arbitration provision anywhere in the agreement. Redline moves the clause to the preferred position (New York law, exclusive New York County courts) while leaving the rest of the sentence structure intact; Delaware, California, or England and Wales/London remains available as a fallback if Garman pushes back.

input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) bars assignment by either party without the other's written consent, with no reasonableness standard and no carve-out permitting Sparkling to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets. Section 3(c) compounds this by prohibiting Sparkling from assigning the Agreement at all except as Garman authorises in writing at its discretion. That is a blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, which is walk-away territory and fails the fallback (mutual assignment to successors on written notice with consent not unreasonably withheld). No change-of-control provision exists, so Garman has no exit right today; the redline confirms this for the future. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out, the reasonableness standard, a no-assignment-to-a-competitor limit on Garman, and conforms Section 3(c).

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Rule:
ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.
Severity: medium
Category: governing-law
Position — preferred:
Laws of the State of New York; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County.
Position — fallback:
Delaware or California law and courts; or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London.
Position — walk-away:
Vendor's home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad.
Detection guidance:
Find the governing-law clause; extract jurisdiction and dispute forum; note any arbitration seat.
Redline guidance:
Replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; keep the rest of the sentence intact.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The only governing-law/venue provision (§ 20(h)) selects the laws of Nova Scotia (and Canadian law applicable there) with the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts. Nova Scotia is not among the accepted laws (New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales), so the clause fails the fallback on both material terms (governing law and forum). It is not walk-away territory: the forum is our own home province (Sparkling is in Dartmouth, NS, while Garman is in Saskatoon, SK), the jurisdiction grant is non-exclusive, and there is no arbitration provision anywhere in the agreement. Redline moves the clause to the preferred position (New York law, exclusive New York County courts) while leaving the rest of the sentence structure intact; Delaware, California, or England and Wales/London remains available as a fallback if Garman pushes back.

p0146: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.

none

p0146: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling (customer) an unconditional right to terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit cost — 90 days' notice sits at the top of the playbook fallback range (60–90 days) and the absence of any termination fee is better than the fallback cap of three months' fees. Garman has no termination-for-convenience right anywhere in the Agreement: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling on notice under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency/uncured material default under 17(c), and Section 10 maintenance is a renewable one-year term without any Garman right to walk away or suspend at will. Section 17(a) also keeps the licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year lock-in. Noted but not flagged as a deviation: 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund in 17(c)/p0128 applies only on Garman default), which is a sub-element short of the preferred position rather than a failure of the fallback, and fee exposure is limited given the annual maintenance term.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant (at fallback).**

Section 17(b) already gives Sparkling a clean convenience exit — termination "at any time" on 90 days' written notice, with no early-termination fee or penalty. That sits at the top of our fallback notice range (60–90 days) and beats the fallback's tolerance for a fee of up to three months' fees.

On the vendor side, Garman has no convenience right at all: Section 17 allows Garman to terminate only for insolvency events or an uncured material default (17(c)), and the Section 10 maintenance term contains no at-will suspension or walk-away right. Section 17(a) keeps the licence perpetual while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year lock-in to escape.

Noted in the rationale but not redlined: 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund at p0128 is limited to termination for Garman's default). That is a sub-element short of our preferred position, not a fallback failure, and exposure is limited by the annual maintenance term — so no redline was proposed.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) bars assignment by either party without the other's written consent, with no reasonableness standard and no carve-out permitting Sparkling to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets. Section 3(c) compounds this by prohibiting Sparkling from assigning the Agreement at all except as Garman authorises in writing at its discretion. That is a blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, which is walk-away territory and fails the fallback (mutual assignment to successors on written notice with consent not unreasonably withheld). No change-of-control provision exists, so Garman has no exit right today; the redline confirms this for the future. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out, the reasonableness standard, a no-assignment-to-a-competitor limit on Garman, and conforms Section 3(c).

We have also confirmed that Section 3(c) does not cut across this.

Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

paragraphs.text: 2. GRANT OF LICENSE

Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.
3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
Sparkling shall:
(a) not copy the Software except to copy it onto another AS400 at the Authorized Locations and to make copies of the Software at each Authorized Location solely for backup purposes;
(b) not copy any of the Documentation except as required for Sparkling's internal purposes related to Sparkling's use of the Software;
(c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
(d) not reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble the Software;
(e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
(f) take all reasonable precautions to prevent third parties from using

the Work in any way that would constitute a breach of this Agreement including, without limitation, such precautions as Sparkling would otherwise take to protect its own proprietary software or hardware or information; and
4. DELIVERY, INSTALLATION AND DATA CONVERSION

(a) In accordance with Schedule "C," Garman has delivered the required number of copies of the executable object code of the Software to those Authorized Locations (together with copies of the Documentation as is reasonably required by Sparkling to operate the Software in the manner contemplated hereunder) and installed the Software on the applicable AS400's at each Authorized Location. The installation of the Software at each existing Authorized Location shall be deemed to be completed including contracted changes and has been properly installed, is in good working order. Modifications and changes shall fall within the 60 day testing period at which time they are deemed to be completed and has been properly installed, is in good working order.

(b) For Future Installations and Conversions at an existing or new Authorized Location, Garman shall be available for Contracting required installation and conversion tasks as reasonably required, in consultation with and with the reasonable assistance of Sparkling, including conversion of Sparkling's data, as more particularly described in Schedule "D," from its current electronic form into a form suitable for processing with the Software and as required for the testing of the Software and for use of the Software as contemplated hereunder.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant at the preferred position. There is no automatic renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "automatically renew" and "renew" return only p0065, under which maintenance runs "For a renewable one-year term" — a 12-month term extendable only by the parties' affirmative agreement — and the licence itself is perpetual so long as fees are paid (p0117). That matches the preferred position of renewal by mutual agreement on a 12-month term.

The ninety (90) day figure in p0118 is not a non-renewal notice window: it is Sparkling's own termination-for-convenience right ("Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman"). It is a customer exit right that benefits us, it is not a condition on renewal, and it belongs to a termination rule rather than this one, so it is not counted against the ≤60-day notice-window parameter.

Two sub-elements fall short of ideal drafting but are minor and noted rather than flagged: there is no express cap on renewal-period maintenance fee uplift (fees are simply "in accordance with the Fee Schedule"), and there is no vendor renewal reminder. We would pursue the CPI/3% uplift cap in the Fee Schedule negotiation rather than by redline here.

Original paragraphs:
p0065: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
p0117: (a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.
p0118: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.

**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, assignment).**

- **Section 20(d)** (p0142) prohibits assignment by either party without the other's written consent — no reasonableness standard, no affiliate carve-out, no successor/M&A carve-out.
- **Section 3(c)** (p0033) is worse and one-sided: Sparkling may not assign the Agreement at all "except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing," i.e. in Garman's absolute discretion.

Together these amount to a blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out — walk-away territory under the rule, and short of the fallback (mutual assignment to successors on notice, consent not unreasonably withheld). There is no change-of-control provision anywhere in the document, so Garman currently has no exit or re-pricing right on our change of control; the redline locks that in expressly.

Redline (validated, preferred position): adds a reasonableness standard on consent, a carve-out letting Sparkling assign to affiliates or a successor by merger/acquisition/sale of substantially all assets on written notice, a bar on Garman assigning to a competitor of ours, and a confirmation that a change of control of Sparkling is not an assignment and triggers no Garman termination, suspension or re-pricing right. Section 3(c) is conformed so the licence restrictions no longer cut across Section 20(d).

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 20(d) bars assignment by either party without the other's written consent, with no reasonableness standard and no carve-out permitting Sparkling to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets. Section 3(c) compounds this by prohibiting Sparkling from assigning the Agreement at all except as Garman authorises in writing at its discretion. That is a blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, which is walk-away territory and fails the fallback (mutual assignment to successors on written notice with consent not unreasonably withheld). No change-of-control provision exists, so Garman has no exit right today; the redline confirms this for the future. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out, the reasonableness standard, a no-assignment-to-a-competitor limit on Garman, and conforms Section 3(c).

Original paragraphs:
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, provided that (i) Sparkling may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the consent of Garman to any of its affiliates or to any successor by way of merger, amalgamation, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business, on written notice to Garman, and (ii) Garman may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of Sparkling. No change of control of Sparkling shall constitute an assignment of this Agreement or give rise to any right of Garman to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
p0033: (c) not transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing or as permitted under Section 20(d);

Comment:
[Playbook] We have added the customary carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and a reasonableness standard on consent (with no assignment by Garman to a competitor of ours), since our playbook does not accept a blanket bar on our ability to assign in a corporate reorganisation or M&A transaction. We have also confirmed that Section 3(c) does not cut across this.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: Compliant at the fallback; no redline proposed. (1) Customer convenience right is present in substance: Section 17(b) (p0118) lets Sparkling terminate "at any time" on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, subject only to ceasing use and certifying return/destruction of the Software. It does not use the label "for convenience" or "without cause", but no cause, default, breach or other trigger is required, so the right is unconditional — substance controls over phrasing, and any deterministic keyword check on "for convenience"/"without cause" is a wording artefact here. (2) Notice period of 90 days sits at the top of the playbook fallback range (60-90 days). (3) No early-termination fee, penalty, forfeiture or accelerated-payment obligation attaches to Section 17(b), which is better than the fallback's tolerance of a fee up to three months' fees. (4) No Vendor convenience right exists anywhere: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency events / material default uncured after thirty days (17(c), p0128), and the Section 10 maintenance term (renewable one-year) contains no Garman right to walk away, suspend or decline service at will — so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience termination on under 90 days' notice) is absent. (5) Section 17(a) (p0117) keeps the Agreement and licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year committed lock-in from which Sparkling needs an exit. Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted as observations only and not escalated: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (the fee-return remedy at p0128 applies only on termination for Garman's default). Fee exposure is limited by the annual maintenance term, so these are minor gaps against preferred rather than failures of the fallback.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Category: term-termination

Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). Confidential Information means all data and information related to the business and management of either party, including proprietary and trade secrets, technology and accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such Confidential Information shall not include data or information which:
(a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;
(b) is already in the rightful possession of the other party prior to its receipt from the other party;
(c) is independently developed by the other party;
(d) is lawfully obtained by the other party from a third party;
(e) is disclosed as required by law; or
(f) is disclosed to professional advisors in confidence.

ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.

Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

**Finding repaired and resubmitted: compliant (at fallback), no redline.**

The substance of the finding is unchanged — the verifier confirmed the classification and confirmed that no redline and no counterparty comment is the expected output. What I strengthened was the rationale, so the record now expressly disposes of the failed deterministic check rather than leaving it unexplained:

- **Customer convenience right is present in substance.** Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate "at any time" on 90 calendar days' written notice, conditioned only on ceasing use and certifying return/destruction. No cause, breach or other trigger is required. The clause simply never uses the words "for convenience" or "without cause," which is why a keyword check would misfire.
- **Notice sits at the top of the fallback range** (60–90 days).
- **No early-termination fee or penalty** attaches to 17(b) — better than the fallback's tolerance of up to three months' fees.
- **No Vendor convenience right anywhere.** Termination is limited to Sparkling under 17(b) or either party for insolvency/uncured 30-day default (17(c), p0128); the annual maintenance term in Section 10 gives Garman no at-will exit or suspension. The walk-away trigger is therefore absent.
- **No committed lock-in.** Section 17(a) keeps the licence perpetual while fees are paid.

Sub-elements short of preferred — 90 days rather than 30, and no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund at p0128 is confined to Garman default) — remain recorded as observations, consistent with the playbook's instruction not to escalate minor gaps against preferred into deviations.
