Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant at the fallback; no redline proposed. (1) Customer convenience right is present in substance: Section 17(b) (p0118) lets Sparkling terminate "at any time" on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, subject only to ceasing use and certifying return/destruction of the Software. It does not use the label "for convenience" or "without cause", but no cause, default, breach or other trigger is required, so the right is unconditional — substance controls over phrasing, and any deterministic keyword check on "for convenience"/"without cause" is a wording artefact here. (2) Notice period of 90 days sits at the top of the playbook fallback range (60-90 days). (3) No early-termination fee, penalty, forfeiture or accelerated-payment obligation attaches to Section 17(b), which is better than the fallback's tolerance of a fee up to three months' fees. (4) No Vendor convenience right exists anywhere: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency events / material default uncured after thirty days (17(c), p0128), and the Section 10 maintenance term (renewable one-year) contains no Garman right to walk away, suspend or decline service at will — so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience termination on under 90 days' notice) is absent. (5) Section 17(a) (p0117) keeps the Agreement and licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year committed lock-in from which Sparkling needs an exit. Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted as observations only and not escalated: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (the fee-return remedy at p0128 applies only on termination for Garman's default). Fee exposure is limited by the annual maintenance term, so these are minor gaps against preferred rather than failures of the fallback.

Original paragraphs:
p0117: (a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.
p0118: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
p0128: this Agreement may be terminated by the other party. If this Agreement is terminated by Sparkling, due to Garman's default, the license herein granted shall continue, but shall be converted to a perpetual license pursuant to which Sparkling shall not be required to pay any further fees to Garman hereunder, and Garman shall immediately return all fees paid under this Agreement for services

ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence

Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.

Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.

Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

paragraphs.text: 17. TERM AND TERMINATION

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
(c) If either party:
(1) makes an assignment in bankruptcy or is adjudicated a bankrupt;
(2) makes a general assignment for the benefit of its creditors;

(3) has a receiver, administrator or manager of its property, assets or undertaking appointed in such circumstances as would in the reasonable discretion of the other party, detrimentally affect such other party's rights under this Agreement;

Sparkling: SPARKLING SPRING WATER GROUP LIMITED 19 Fielding Avenue Dartmouth, NS B3B 1C9

Any notice sent by personal delivery shall be deemed to be given on the day of its delivery provided it is received during regular business hours on a business day, and if it is not received as such then it shall be deemed to be given on the next business day. Any notices sent by facsimile transmission shall be deemed to be given on the day of transmission if received during regular business hours on a business day, and if it is not received as such then it shall be deemed to be given on the next business day.

(c) Unless otherwise permitted by this Agreement, no waiver of any part of this Agreement shall be binding unless executed in writing by both parties. No waiver of any part of this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of any other part or a continuing waiver unless otherwise agreed to in writing by both parties.
(d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

(e) The parties are acting as independent contractors under this Agreement and not as agents or representatives of the other and not as partners or joint ventures. Neither party shall enter into any agreement or commitment on behalf of the other without the written consent of the other.

(f) If either party is delayed or prevented from exercising its obligations or making deliveries in accordance with this Agreement due to circumstances beyond the reasonable control of that party including without limitation, strikes, lockouts, labor disputes, fire, explosion, act of god or other similar causes, then such failure to meet obligations or make deliveries shall not be a breach of this Agreement.

(g) Each of the provisions contained in this Agreement is distinct and severable. If one or more of the provisions of this Agreement is found to be illegal or unenforceable, this Agreement shall not be rendered inoperative or invalid but the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

(h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
(i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.

Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant at the preferred position; no redline and no counterparty comment.

(1) No auto-renewal exists. Searches for "automatically renew" return nothing; the only renewal reference is p0065, under which maintenance runs "For a renewable one-year term" — a 12-month term extendable only by the parties' affirmative agreement. The licence itself "shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid" (p0117). There is therefore no rolling term, no multi-year renewal, and no "unless notice ... days prior" condition to compute. This is the preferred position: renewal by mutual agreement on a 12-month term.

(2) The ninety-day figure is not a non-renewal notice window. It appears only in p0118 — "Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman" — which is our own termination-for-convenience right. It binds Garman to accept our exit, benefits our party, and is not a condition on renewal, so it is excluded from the ≤60-day parameter and belongs to a termination rule instead.

(3) Minor sub-elements short of ideal drafting, noted not flagged: no CPI/3% cap on renewal-period maintenance fee uplift (fees are simply "in accordance with the Fee Schedule") and no 60-day vendor renewal reminder. Per the classification semantics these are not deviations; we would raise the uplift cap in the Fee Schedule negotiation rather than by redlining Section 10.

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
A Vendor IP infringement indemnity is present. Section 13 (continuing at p0090) has Garman represent and warrant that it owns or controls all rights necessary to grant the licence and that no lien, encumbrance or third-party right will interfere with Sparkling's rights, and then provides that "Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless" from all Losses — expressly including amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and investigation costs — arising from breach of that warranty. The same paragraph deals directly with the infringement scenario ("If the Work or any portion thereof is held to constitute an infringement of another Person's rights, and use thereof is enjoined"), obliging Garman at its own expense to procure the right to use the infringing element, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify the Work so it is non-infringing without material loss of functionality (p0091–p0093). That is a Vendor IP indemnity with the usual remedy ladder, i.e. the rule's fallback position. Direction is correct: the indemnity runs from Garman to us, and there is no reverse or one-way Sparkling indemnity for Garman's software or services anywhere in the agreement, so the walk-away case does not arise. Section 15 is also better than the fallback: the cap and the consequential/indirect damages exclusion "shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14", leaving the IP indemnity uncapped rather than subject to a 3x super-cap. Recorded as internal evidence only, short of the preferred position and not flagged as deviations: no express "defend"/control-of-defence and cooperation mechanic, no refund remedy if none of (a)-(c) can be achieved, indemnity limited to IP/title matters (no breach-of-law, Customer Data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs), affiliates not named as beneficiaries, and a tight ten-calendar-day notice obligation on us. Compliant at the fallback; no redline proposed.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Compliant at the fallback; no redline and no counterparty comment. Customer convenience right is present in substance: Section 17(b) (p0118) lets Sparkling terminate "at any time" on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, conditioned only on ceasing use and certifying return or destruction of the Software. No cause, breach, default or other trigger is required, so the right is unconditional; the clause simply does not carry the labels "for convenience" or "without cause", which is why a keyword-based check reports "Customer convenience termination present: failed". That is a wording artefact and substance controls. Ninety days sits at the top of the fallback notice range (60-90 days), and no early-termination fee, penalty, forfeiture or acceleration attaches to the exit, which is better than the fallback tolerance of a fee up to three months' fees. No Vendor convenience right exists anywhere: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency events and material default uncured after thirty days (17(c), p0128), and the renewable one-year maintenance term in Section 10 gives Garman no at-will right to exit, suspend or decline service, so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience termination on fewer than 90 days' notice) is absent. Section 17(a) (p0117) also keeps the Agreement and licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year committed term from which Sparkling needs an exit. Shortfalls against the preferred position are recorded as observations only, not escalated: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and 17(b) contains no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (the fee-return remedy at p0128 applies only on termination for Garman's default), with prepayment exposure limited by the annual maintenance cycle.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

**Finding: compliant (at fallback).**

Section 17(b) already gives Sparkling a clean convenience exit — termination "at any time" on 90 days' written notice, with no early-termination fee or penalty. That sits at the top of our fallback notice range (60–90 days) and beats the fallback's tolerance for a fee of up to three months' fees.

On the vendor side, Garman has no convenience right at all: Section 17 allows Garman to terminate only for insolvency events or an uncured material default (17(c)), and the Section 10 maintenance term contains no at-will suspension or walk-away right. Section 17(a) keeps the licence perpetual while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year lock-in to escape.

Noted in the rationale but not redlined: 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund at p0128 is limited to termination for Garman's default). Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.

Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant at the fallback; no redline and no counterparty comment. Customer convenience right is present in substance: Section 17(b) (p0118) lets Sparkling terminate "at any time" on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, conditioned only on ceasing use and certifying return or destruction of the Software. No cause, breach, default or other trigger is required, so the right is unconditional; the clause simply does not carry the labels "for convenience" or "without cause", which is why a keyword-based check reports "Customer convenience termination present: failed". That is a wording artefact and substance controls. Ninety days sits at the top of the fallback notice range (60-90 days), and no early-termination fee, penalty, forfeiture or acceleration attaches to the exit, which is better than the fallback tolerance of a fee up to three months' fees. No Vendor convenience right exists anywhere: Section 17 permits termination only by Sparkling under 17(b) or by either party for insolvency events and material default uncured after thirty days (17(c), p0128), and the renewable one-year maintenance term in Section 10 gives Garman no at-will right to exit, suspend or decline service, so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience termination on fewer than 90 days' notice) is absent. Section 17(a) (p0117) also keeps the Agreement and licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year committed term from which Sparkling needs an exit. Shortfalls against the preferred position are recorded as observations only, not escalated: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and 17(b) contains no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (the fee-return remedy at p0128 applies only on termination for Garman's default), with prepayment exposure limited by the annual maintenance cycle.

Original paragraphs:
p0117: (a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.
p0118: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
p0128: this Agreement may be terminated by the other party. If this Agreement is terminated by Sparkling, due to Garman's default, the license herein granted shall continue, but shall be converted to a perpetual license pursuant to which Sparkling shall not be required to pay any further fees to Garman hereunder, and Garman shall immediately return all fees paid under this Agreement for services

paragraphs.text: 19. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES

During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.
PAGE 10
Garman: GARMAN ROUTING SYSTEMS, INC #1 - 502 45th Street West Saskatoon, SK S7L 6H2
Sparkling: SPARKLING SPRING WATER GROUP LIMITED 19 Fielding Avenue Dartmouth, NS B3B 1C9

Any notice sent by personal delivery shall be deemed to be given on the day of its delivery provided it is received during regular business hours on a business day, and if it is not received as such then it shall be deemed to be given on the next business day. Any notices sent by facsimile transmission shall be deemed to be given on the day of transmission if received during regular business hours on a business day, and if it is not received as such then it shall be deemed to be given on the next business day.

(c) Unless otherwise permitted by this Agreement, no waiver of any part of this Agreement shall be binding unless executed in writing by both parties. No waiver of any part of this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of any other part or a continuing waiver unless otherwise agreed to in writing by both parties.
(d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

(e) The parties are acting as independent contractors under this Agreement and not as agents or representatives of the other and not as partners or joint ventures. Neither party shall enter into any agreement or commitment on behalf of the other without the written consent of the other.

(f) If either party is delayed or prevented from exercising its obligations or making deliveries in accordance with this Agreement due to circumstances beyond the reasonable control of that party including without limitation, strikes, lockouts, labor disputes, fire, explosion, act of god or other similar causes, then such failure to meet obligations or make deliveries shall not be a breach of this Agreement.

(g) Each of the provisions contained in this Agreement is distinct and severable. If one or more of the provisions of this Agreement is found to be illegal or unenforceable, this Agreement shall not be rendered inoperative or invalid but the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

(h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
(i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.

input.rationale: The grant is perpetual (Section 17(a): in effect perpetually while fees are paid) and not revocable at Garman's discretion, and it already extends to Sparkling's affiliated companies, so it is not walk-away territory. However it fails the fallback on two material terms: it is expressly "non-transferable" with assignment barred without Garman's consent (Sections 3(c) and 20(d)), leaving no right to transfer the licence to a successor in an M&A transaction; and contractors or outsourced providers using the Software on our behalf are not covered, with any sublicence available only at Garman's discretion. The redline makes the minimal edits to reach the preferred position: contractor use on our behalf at the Authorized Locations, and assignment of the agreement and licence to a successor on a merger or sale of the business, while preserving Garman's consent right for all other assignments and the Authorized Locations limits.

proposal.summary: Extend licence to contractors acting on our behalf and permit transfer of the licence to a successor in an M&A transaction.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the licence to contractors and outsourced providers using the Software on our behalf, and allowed the licence to move with the business to a successor in a merger or sale, consistent with our licence-scope position. The licence remains restricted to the Authorized Locations and Garman's consent right is preserved for all other assignments.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

No Vendor convenience right appears in the cited provisions; termination is otherwise limited to insolvency/material default, so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience on <90 days) is absent.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is plausibly a keyword artefact — the clause lacks the labels 'for convenience'/'without cause' but is substantively an at-will right — and substance properly controls here.

Shortfalls against the preferred position (90 days rather than 30; no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees in 17(b)) are correctly recorded as observations rather than escalated as deviations, consistent with the classification rules.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 13 vests ownership of all IP in the Work in Garman, expressly including the "Modifications" — which are the bespoke changes set out in Schedule "D" that we commission and pay for. Our only rights in them come from the Section 2 licence, which is non-exclusive, non-transferable, confined to Authorized Locations and (per Section 3) carries no right to modify or sublicense; that falls short of the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables. Separately, the Agreement contains no statement that we retain rights in our own data, even though Garman converts and handles Sparkling's data under Section 4(b) (confidentiality in Section 14 protects but does not allocate ownership). Nothing assigns our IP or data to Garman, so this is not walk-away territory, and Garman's ownership of the Software platform and its Improvements is acceptable. The minimal redline adds a Sparkling data-ownership sentence and a licence back over the bespoke Modifications; Section 17(a) already makes the licence perpetual while fees are paid.

proposal.summary: Add Sparkling data ownership and a perpetual licence back to bespoke Modifications in § 13
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added confirmation that Sparkling retains all rights in its own data and materials and that nothing in this Agreement assigns our IP or data to Garman, together with a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use and modify the Schedule "D" Modifications developed for us. We are content for Garman to own its Software platform and its Improvements; our playbook simply requires customer data ownership and a licence back to deliverables we pay for.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in and to Sparkling's data and any materials, information or content supplied or generated by Sparkling (including data converted pursuant to Section 4), and nothing in this Agreement operates to transfer or assign any of Sparkling's intellectual property or data to Garman. Garman grants to Sparkling a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and have modified the Modifications, and any other deliverables developed specifically for Sparkling under this Agreement, for Sparkling's internal business purposes.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

input.rationale: Section 13 vests ownership of all IP in the Work in Garman, expressly including the "Modifications" — which are the bespoke changes set out in Schedule "D" that we commission and pay for. Our only rights in them come from the Section 2 licence, which is non-exclusive, non-transferable, confined to Authorized Locations and (per Section 3) carries no right to modify or sublicense; that falls short of the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables. Separately, the Agreement contains no statement that we retain rights in our own data, even though Garman converts and handles Sparkling's data under Section 4(b) (confidentiality in Section 14 protects but does not allocate ownership). Nothing assigns our IP or data to Garman, so this is not walk-away territory, and Garman's ownership of the Software platform and its Improvements is acceptable. The minimal redline adds a Sparkling data-ownership sentence and a licence back over the bespoke Modifications; Section 17(a) already makes the licence perpetual while fees are paid.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

Category: audit

No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The grant is perpetual (Section 17(a): in effect perpetually while fees are paid) and not revocable at Garman's discretion, and it already extends to Sparkling's affiliated companies, so it is not walk-away territory. However it fails the fallback on two material terms: it is expressly "non-transferable" with assignment barred without Garman's consent (Sections 3(c) and 20(d)), leaving no right to transfer the licence to a successor in an M&A transaction; and contractors or outsourced providers using the Software on our behalf are not covered, with any sublicence available only at Garman's discretion. The redline makes the minimal edits to reach the preferred position: contractor use on our behalf at the Authorized Locations, and assignment of the agreement and licence to a successor on a merger or sale of the business, while preserving Garman's consent right for all other assignments and the Authorized Locations limits.

Original paragraphs:
p0028: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0028: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling, affiliated companies of Sparkling and contractors and outsourced service providers acting on behalf of Sparkling or such affiliated companies, in each case operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as permitted by Section 20(d) or as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, except that either party may assign this Agreement, including the licence granted under Section 2, to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business without such consent.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have extended the licence to contractors and outsourced providers using the Software on our behalf, and allowed the licence to move with the business to a successor in a merger or sale, consistent with our licence-scope position. The licence remains restricted to the Authorized Locations and Garman's consent right is preserved for all other assignments.

paragraphs.text: 15. LIMITATION OF GARMAN'S LIABILITY

The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use. The parties agree that the limitation of liability in this paragraph reflects the allocation of risk between the parties and the price of the licenced Software. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322

ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, stipulated-damages, late-payment interest or minimum/early-termination charge payable by Sparkling. Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule, and Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate at will on 90 days' notice with no termination fee or remaining-value payment; searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty" and "interest" returned nothing customer-payable, and the non-solicitation covenant (Section 19) carries no placement fee. On termination for Garman's default, the money flows to us (perpetual licence, no further fees, refund of prepaid fees for services not rendered). This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is warranted.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

**Finding: compliant (no audit right against us).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection or licence-verification right binding Sparkling. I checked:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — substantive use restrictions only (copying, sublicensing, reverse engineering), with no verification or reporting mechanic attached.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — only time-of-essence and notices.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises*, *access*, *remote* — the only hits are Garman's telephone support access **to** Sparkling (§ 10) and mutual confidentiality (§ 14, "accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party").

Because no audit right exists, there is nothing to constrain on frequency, notice, business hours, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access. That outcome is better than the playbook's preferred position and benefits us, so this is recorded as compliant with no redline. Worth noting for negotiation awareness only: if Garman later proposes a verification clause, we should insert the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access).

content.text:
**Finding: compliant (no audit right against us).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection or licence-verification right binding Sparkling. I checked:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — substantive use restrictions only (copying, sublicensing, reverse engineering), with no verification or reporting mechanic attached.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — only time-of-essence and notices.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises*, *access*, *remote* — the only hits are Garman's telephone support access **to** Sparkling (§ 10) and mutual confidentiality (§ 14, "accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party").

Because no audit right exists, there is nothing to constrain on frequency, notice, business hours, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access. That outcome is better than the playbook's preferred position and benefits us, so this is recorded as compliant with no redline. Worth noting for negotiation awareness only: if Garman later proposes a verification clause, we should insert the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access).

**Finding: compliant (no audit right against us).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection or licence-verification right binding Sparkling. I checked:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — substantive use restrictions only (copying, sublicensing, reverse engineering), with no verification or reporting mechanic attached.

Because no audit right exists, there is nothing to constrain on frequency, notice, business hours, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access. (a) Time shall be of the essence with respect to all matters under this Agreement.

input.rationale: Section 12 gives an express conformance warranty running through the acceptance period, a full year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and thereafter for as long as Maintenance Services continue — at or above the preferred 12-month software warranty. A real remedy exists: Garman must repair non-conforming Software at no charge under the Software Repair Service (§10(c)/p0077), and a full refund of all amounts paid is available if the Software is rejected on acceptance (§8(b)). Critically, there is no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere in the agreement, so nothing swallows the express warranty, and §15 preserves direct damages. Sub-elements short of the preferred wording — no separate professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, no express compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranties, and repair rather than an express repair/replace/refund election — are noted but are not material deviations given the longer-than-preferred period and the refund path on rejection. No redline proposed.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.

input.quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
input.rationale: Section 12 gives an express conformance warranty running through the acceptance period, a full year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and thereafter for as long as Maintenance Services continue — at or above the preferred 12-month software warranty. A real remedy exists: Garman must repair non-conforming Software at no charge under the Software Repair Service (§10(c)/p0077), and a full refund of all amounts paid is available if the Software is rejected on acceptance (§8(b)). Critically, there is no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere in the agreement, so nothing swallows the express warranty, and §15 preserves direct damages. Sub-elements short of the preferred wording — no separate professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, no express compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranties, and repair rather than an express repair/replace/refund election — are noted but are not material deviations given the longer-than-preferred period and the refund path on rejection. No redline proposed.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 12 gives an express conformance warranty running through the acceptance period, a full year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and thereafter for as long as Maintenance Services continue — at or above the preferred 12-month software warranty. A real remedy exists: Garman must repair non-conforming Software at no charge under the Software Repair Service (§10(c)/p0077), and a full refund of all amounts paid is available if the Software is rejected on acceptance (§8(b)). Critically, there is no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere in the agreement, so nothing swallows the express warranty, and §15 preserves direct damages. Sub-elements short of the preferred wording — no separate professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, no express compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranties, and repair rather than an express repair/replace/refund election — are noted but are not material deviations given the longer-than-preferred period and the refund path on rejection. No redline proposed.

The parties agree that the limitation of liability in this paragraph reflects the allocation of risk between the parties and the price of the licenced Software. reasons: Classification is correct: Section 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work expressly including the bespoke 'Modifications', and the only Customer right (Section 2, read with the Authorized Locations limitation) is a non-exclusive, non-transferable use licence with no right to modify — this fails the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use/modify deliverables, so it is not an acceptable-fallback over-flag.

Second limb is also supported: no provision allocates ownership of Sparkling's data even though Garman converts and processes it under Section 4(b); confidentiality (Section 14) does not allocate ownership, so a data-ownership sentence is warranted under the rule's redline guidance.

Redline is directionally correct and additive: it leaves Garman's ownership of the Software platform and Improvements intact (permitted by the rule), adds a Customer Data / no-assignment sentence, and adds a licence back over the paid-for Modifications — the smallest edit that reaches the fallback, consistent with the 'add the licence-back' guidance.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position, and does not misstate what changed; deterministic checks confirm no assignment of Customer IP/data to Vendor remains.

Minor shortfall worth noting but not disqualifying: the granted licence covers 'use, modify and have modified ... for Sparkling's internal business purposes' and omits an express sublicensing right contemplated by the fallback; consider adding 'and sublicense (including to affiliates and service providers)' if the counterparty reopens the clause.

Second limb is also supported: no provision allocates ownership of Sparkling's data even though Garman converts and processes it under Section 4(b); confidentiality (Section 14) does not allocate ownership, so a data-ownership sentence is warranted under the rule's redline guidance. Redline is directionally correct and additive: it leaves Garman's ownership of the Software platform and Improvements intact (permitted by the rule), adds a Customer Data / no-assignment sentence, and adds a licence back over the paid-for Modifications — the smallest edit that reaches the fallback, consistent with the 'add the licence-back' guidance. Minor shortfall worth noting but not disqualifying: the granted licence covers 'use, modify and have modified ... for Sparkling's internal business purposes' and omits an express sublicensing right contemplated by the fallback; consider adding 'and sublicense (including to affiliates and service providers)' if the counterparty reopens the clause.
