How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No audit, inspection, licence-verification or system-access right runs against Sparkling anywhere in the Agreement. Regex and literal searches for audit / inspect / verif / examin / records / premises / access / remote, plus full reads of § 3 (Restrictions on Use), § 14 (Confidentiality) and § 20 (General Matters), return no such right: § 3 imposes substantive use restrictions only, with no verification, reporting or self-certification mechanic; § 14 is a mutual confidentiality provision whose reference to "accounting records for which access is obtained" is a definitional carve-in, not a grant of access; and the only "access" in § 10 is Garman's telephone support provided to us. The single examination right in the document (§ 16 escrow, p0114) runs in our favour, permitting Sparkling and its independent experts to examine and test the escrow materials for Garman's compliance. Because there is no audit right binding us, there is nothing to constrain on frequency, notice, business hours, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access, and the outcome is better than the playbook preferred position. The failed deterministic check ("audit frequency limited") is a direct consequence of the total absence of an audit clause rather than a defect in the drafting: the AUDIT rule exists to cap a Vendor-favourable right, so its absence benefits our party and is correctly treated as compliant rather than missing. No redline or comment is proposed, since raising the point would invite Garman to introduce a verification right we do not currently owe.

14. CONFIDENTIALITY

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). Confidential Information means all data and information related to the business and management of either party, including proprietary and trade secrets, technology and accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such Confidential Information shall not include data or information which:
(a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge or volume cap on us. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay", "non-cancellable" and "volume" return nothing relevant (the only "commitment" hit, p0143, is the no-agency clause). Fees are payable only as set out in the Fee Schedule (§11/p0084), with additional fees arising only if we choose to use the Software beyond the Authorized Locations (§2/p0028). Maintenance runs in a renewable one-year term rather than a fixed multi-year obligation (§10/p0065), and we may terminate the whole Agreement for convenience on ninety (90) days' notice (§17(b)/p0118), so there is no locked-in spend without an exit. This meets the preferred position (fees for usage or ordered services only). Note: the commercial exposure sits in Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule), which is not reproduced in this text — worth confirming the schedule itself carries no committed user/location counts or minimum annual maintenance spend.

**Finding: compliant (no audit right against us).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection or licence-verification right binding Sparkling. I checked:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — substantive use restrictions only (copying, sublicensing, reverse engineering), with no verification or reporting mechanic attached.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — only time-of-essence and notices.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises*, *access*, *remote* — the only hits are Garman's telephone support access **to** Sparkling (§ 10) and mutual confidentiality (§ 14, "accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party").

Because no audit right exists, there is nothing to constrain on frequency, notice, business hours, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access. That outcome is better than the playbook's preferred position and benefits us, so this is recorded as compliant with no redline. Worth noting for negotiation awareness only: if Garman later proposes a verification clause, we should insert the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access).

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

The document contains no take-or-pay exposure for us:

- **No commitment language anywhere** — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay", "non-cancellable", "volume" return nothing on point (the sole "commitment" hit is the no-agency clause at p0143).
- **§11 Fees (p0084)** — fees payable only as set out in the Fee Schedule; **§2 (p0028)** makes additional fees contingent on *our* election to use the Software beyond Authorized Locations.
- **§10 (p0065)** — maintenance runs on a renewable one-year term, not a fixed multi-year obligation.
- **§17(b) (p0118)** — we hold an unconditional termination-for-convenience right on 90 days' notice, so even the perpetual fee-paying structure in §17(a) carries a clean exit.

This sits at the **preferred** position (fees for usage or ordered services only), not merely the fallback.

ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
A Vendor-to-Customer IP infringement indemnity is present and sits at the rule's fallback position, so no redline is proposed. Evidence: (1) the clause is headed "13. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY" (p0087); (2) the operative indemnity quoted above (p0090) is given by Garman in our favour and covers all Losses, expressly including amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and investigation costs; (3) its trigger is Garman's warranty in the immediately preceding sentence that "it owns or controls all rights necessary to grant the rights to Sparkling" and that no "lien, encumbrance, security interest or other rights against the Work" will interfere with our rights — i.e. an IP title/non-infringement warranty; and (4) the same paragraph then governs the infringement scenario itself: "If the Work or any portion thereof is held to constitute an infringement of another Person's rights, and use thereof is enjoined, Garman shall, at its election and expense", procure the right to use the infringing element, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify the Work so the infringing portion is non-infringing without material loss of functionality (p0091-p0093). That is a Vendor IP indemnity with the usual remedy ladder. Direction is correct: the obligation runs from Vendor to us, and there is no reverse or one-way Sparkling indemnity for Garman's software or services anywhere in the agreement, so walk-away territory does not arise. Section 15 is more favourable than the fallback's 3x super-cap: the direct-damages-only limitation and the consequential-damages exclusion "shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14" (p0105), leaving this indemnity uncapped. p0090: Garman represents and warrants that it owns or controls all rights necessary to grant the rights to Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement and that there are not, nor will there be, any lien, encumbrance, security interest or other rights against the Work which will interfere in any way with the rights granted to Sparkling. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use. **Final finding: AUDIT — compliant. No redline, no comment.**

The repair is complete; the substance was already correct and the verifier confirmed each element, so I tightened the rationale rather than altering the conclusion.

Basis for the finding:
- **No audit right against us exists.** Literal and regex sweeps (*audit, inspect, verif, examin, right to enter, books, records, premises, access, remote*) plus full reads of § 3, § 14 and § 20 turn up nothing binding Sparkling.
- **§ 3 (p0029–p0035)** contains substantive use restrictions only — no verification, reporting or self-certification mechanic attached.
- **§ 14 (p0095)** — "accounting records for which access is obtained" is definitional scoping within a mutual confidentiality clause, not a grant of access. The only § 10 "access" is Garman's telephone support flowing *to* us.
- **§ 16 escrow (p0114)** is the sole examination right in the document and it runs **in our favour**.

Why no edit: the AUDIT rule caps a Vendor-favourable right, so its absence places us at or better than the preferred position. Inserting frequency/notice/cost parameters would create the very obligation the rule is designed to limit. The failed deterministic check ("audit frequency limited") is an artefact of there being no audit clause to measure, not a defect.

Negotiation note only, not raised with Garman: if a verification right is later proposed, hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct system access.

Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.

Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No audit, inspection, licence-verification or system-access right runs against Sparkling anywhere in the Agreement. Literal and regex searches (audit / inspect / verif / examin / right to enter / books / records / premises / access / remote), plus full reads of § 3 (Restrictions on Use), § 14 (Confidentiality) and § 20 (General Matters), return none: § 3 (p0029-p0035) imposes substantive use restrictions only, with no verification, reporting or self-certification mechanic; the "accounting records for which access is obtained" wording in p0095 is definitional scoping inside a mutual confidentiality clause, not a grant of access; and the only "access" in § 10 is Garman's telephone support supplied to us. The sole examination right in the document runs in our favour: under § 16 escrow (p0114) Sparkling may itself or through independent experts examine and test the escrow materials for Garman's compliance. With no audit right binding us there is nothing to constrain as to frequency, notice, business hours, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access, so the position is at or better than the playbook preferred position. The failed deterministic check ("audit frequency limited") is a heuristic artefact of the total absence of an audit clause, not evidence of an unconstrained audit right; because AUDIT exists to cap a Vendor-favourable right, its absence benefits our party and is compliant rather than missing. No redline or comment is proposed: raising the point would invite Garman to introduce a verification right we do not currently owe. If Garman later tables one, we should hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

The rule's fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export) is therefore also unmet, so we insert a new Section 17(d) at the preferred position: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, return of our data within thirty days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Sparkling, the Customer)  
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Software License and Maintenance Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is broadly workable for us — the licence is perpetual while fees are paid, there is no auto-renewal, no exclusivity, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no liquidated damages and no audit right running against us, and we hold an unconditional 90-day exit right. The express warranty in § 12 is longer than our preferred position and is not undercut by any "AS IS" disclaimer.

The issues that require negotiation are concentrated in three areas. First, **liability**: § 15 contains no monetary cap at all, leaving our own direct-damages exposure unlimited, which fails both the preferred and fallback positions. Second, **assignment**: § 20(d) and § 3(c) impose a blanket bar on assignment by us with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out — walk-away territory — and the same restriction also narrows the licence grant under § 2. Third, **exit and risk allocation**: there is no transition assistance or data-return mechanic anywhere in the Agreement, and no vendor insurance requirement, notwithstanding that Garman installs on-premises and converts our data. We also need ownership language for Sparkling data and a licence back over the bespoke Modifications we pay for (§ 13), and a move off Nova Scotia law and venue (§ 20(h)).

Four findings are recorded as **needs review**: in each case the substantive position is at or above the playbook line, and the flag arises from a wording or keyword artefact rather than a drafting gap. We recommend confirming these on the record and not redlining them.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Needs review | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Vendor-to-Customer IP indemnity present and sits at the fallback; uncapped via the § 13/14 carve-out in § 15. Flag is a phrasing artefact (trigger drafted as breach of the ownership/non-infringement warranty). No redline. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman owns all IP in the Work including the bespoke Modifications we commission; our § 2 licence carries no modify/sublicense right, and no clause confirms we retain rights in our own data. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary cap of any kind; direct-damages exposure is unlimited for both parties, including us. Fails preferred and fallback on a material term. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(d); see also § 3(c)) | Blanket consent requirement with no reasonableness standard and no affiliate or successor/M&A carve-out for us. **Walk-away territory.** |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No exclusivity or sole-source obligation on us; grant is non-exclusive. Preferred position met. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | No liquidated damages, penalty, late interest or early-termination charge payable by us. Preferred position met. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Licence is perpetual and covers our affiliates, but is non-transferable (no successor transfer on M&A) and does not cover contractors or outsourced providers acting on our behalf. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction; § 3 is limited to ordinary licence-scope protections. Preferred position met. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Needs review | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17(b) gives us an unconditional exit on 90 days' notice with no fee; no Vendor convenience right exists. Compliant at the fallback; flag is a labelling artefact. No redline. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No audit, inspection or verification right runs against us anywhere; the only examination right (§ 16 escrow) runs in our favour. At or better than preferred. No redline — raising it would invite one. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive Nova Scotia courts; Nova Scotia is not an accepted law, so the clause fails the fallback on both material terms. Not walk-away (home forum, non-exclusive, no arbitration). |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No MFN or MFC obligation on us anywhere. Preferred position met. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap; fees payable per the Fee Schedule only. Preferred position met, subject to confirming Schedule "A". |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Drafted as a mutual **no-hire** reaching "any employee of the other party", with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Fails the fallback despite being mutual and 12 months. **Walk-away territory.** |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Needs review | § 10 Maintenance and Support | No auto-renewal; maintenance is a renewable one-year term by affirmative agreement. The 90-day figure is our own convenience right, not a non-renewal window. Preferred position met. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination | Exit obligations run only on us; no transition assistance, data export or deletion certification anywhere. Fallback (90 days' assistance / 30-day export) also unmet. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Conformance warranty through acceptance, a full year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and while Maintenance continues, with a repair remedy and refund on rejection; no "AS IS" disclaimer. At or above preferred. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Page 10 (§ 20 General Matters) | No insurance or certificate requirement anywhere, notwithstanding on-premises installation and data conversion. **Walk-away territory** per the rule. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These three items are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **Assignment (§ 20(d), § 3(c))** — the blanket prohibition on assignment by us, with no affiliate or successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, is a blocker. We need the affiliate/successor carve-out, consent not unreasonably withheld, a no-assignment-to-a-competitor limit on Garman, and § 3(c) conformed.
2. **Non-solicitation (§ 19)** — a mutual no-hire covering all of the other party's employees, with no carve-outs, is a blocker. We need it converted to a narrow 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and the no-hire deleted.
3. **Vendor insurance (absent)** — the complete absence of any insurance covenant, where Garman installs on-premises and converts our data, is a blocker. We are inserting the model coverage as a new § 20(j), with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback available.

We would also treat the **uncapped liability position in § 15** as close to a condition: as drafted, our own direct-damages exposure is unlimited.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redlines** on the seven items with proposals: § 15 mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims and fees excluded from the cap); § 20(d)/§ 3(c) assignment carve-out; § 19 non-solicit narrowing; new § 20(j) insurance; new § 17(d) transition assistance, 30-day machine-readable data return and certified deletion; § 13 Sparkling data ownership plus perpetual licence back over the bespoke Modifications; § 2 contractor use and successor transfer; § 20(h) New York law and exclusive New York County venue.
2. **Set the negotiation order** — lead with assignment, non-solicitation, insurance and the liability cap; treat governing law as tradeable (Delaware, California, or England and Wales/London remain acceptable fallbacks).
3. **Do not redline the four needs-review items** (indemnity, termination for convenience, audit, renewal).
